te: Taking research all the way to real and commercial use
se: The committee heard the Thailand Science Research and Innovation office (TSRI), the Office of the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation (MHESI) and the professional association of intellectual property and technology transfer managers on technology transfer and commercialising research, such as building an innovation ecosystem, bridging the gap where research is left unused before production, raising professional standards for intellectual property managers, and setting up a central unit to find promising university research and match it with industry.
it: Promoting technology transfer and the commercial use of research (TSRI, Office of the Permanent Secretary of MHESI, AITP)

te: Draft report on education for children with disabilities and disadvantaged children
se: The learning promotion subcommittee reported on its consideration of the draft report “Policy proposals on a model for systematic and sustainable quality education for children with disabilities and disadvantaged children”, prepared by its special education working group, and the higher education subcommittee reported on its work.
it: Draft report with policy proposals on education for children with disabilities and disadvantaged children
Work of the higher education subcommittee

te: Vocational education that meets labour market needs, and lifelong learning for all ages
se: The committee heard the Office of the Vocational Education Commission (OVEC) on managing and developing vocational education to match labour market needs and the national economic and social development plan, and the Department of Learning Encouragement on lifelong learning and learning for qualifications for people of all ages, with a focus on reforming education for careers and jobs that meet industry's needs.
it: Managing and developing vocational education to meet labour market needs (OVEC)
Lifelong learning for people of all ages (Department of Learning Encouragement)

te: Welfare and development of teachers outside OBEC, and results of the Nan visit
se: The Subcommittee on Learning Promotion, Private Education, Special Education and Educational Equality reported on its study of personnel management, development and welfare for teachers such as those under the Department of Learning Encouragement, special education teachers and private school teachers, in line with Section 258 of the Constitution on education. It will request information from the agencies concerned, and it summarised its study visit on this topic in Nan.
it: Personnel management, development and welfare of teachers
Results of the study visit to Nan

te: Results of the United Kingdom visit: vocational education, technology transfer and the National Education Bill
se: The committee summarised its bilateral meeting and study visit to the United Kingdom on 2–8 March 2026, including a large public further education college in London formed from three colleges and serving learners aged 12 to 90, a college of hospitality and cookery, the University of Cambridge's technology transfer office and Oxford University Press. The committee noted, for example, that the new National Education Bill should truly reform learning rather than only reorganise structures.
it: Summary of the bilateral meeting and study visit to the United Kingdom (2–8 March 2026)
The committee's observations, such as on reforming education law

te: Preparing the visit to the United Kingdom, and political parties' education policies (continued)
se: The committee prepared its bilateral meeting and study visit to the United Kingdom on 2–8 March 2026 on four topics: new approaches to vocational education, commercialising research, digital technology in classrooms and education reform, and continued considering the education policies of two political parties.
it: Preparing the bilateral meeting and study visit to the United Kingdom (2–8 March 2026)
Political parties' education policies and directions (continued)

te: Drugs in schools, using research, and political parties' education policies
se: The education and vocational education subcommittee reported information from the Ministry of Education on preventing drug problems in schools, such as OBEC's three measures of prevention, instilling values and suppression, and the TO BE NUMBER ONE project. The higher education subcommittee reported on its work, and the committee considered the education policies of two political parties, which share points such as using technology to reduce barriers to education.
it: Proposals on preventing drug problems in schools (education and vocational education subcommittee)
Work of the higher education subcommittee
Political parties' education policies and directions

te: Safety in schools after an attacker entered a school in Songkhla
se: The committee heard OBEC and the Royal Thai Police on the case of an attacker who entered a school in Hat Yai District, Songkhla, to learn lessons and find measures to keep schools safe, rebuild the confidence of teachers and parents, and consider compensation and benefits for the families of staff who died on duty. It also heard the higher education subcommittee and prepared the visit to the United Kingdom.
it: Measures to keep schools safe and support for staff families (OBEC and the Royal Thai Police)
Work of the higher education subcommittee
Preparing the bilateral meeting in the United Kingdom

te: Learning anywhere, anytime, and preparing a study visit
se: Mr Suthin Kaewpana, First Vice-Chair, presided over the meeting as assigned. The education and vocational education subcommittee reported progress on proposals for flexible education in and outside the school system and lifelong learning (Anywhere Anytime) supported by technology, with information from the Ministry of Education, OBEC, the Office of the Vocational Education Commission, the Department of Learning Encouragement, the Office of the Private Education Commission and the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society. The committee also considered a study visit by the learning promotion subcommittee.
it: Progress of proposals on flexible education and lifelong learning (Anywhere Anytime)
Preparing a study visit by the Subcommittee on Learning Promotion, Private Education, Special Education and Educational Equality

te: The United Kingdom's education system, and preparing for PISA
se: The committee heard the British Council Thailand on the education system of the United Kingdom to prepare for its bilateral meeting. The education and vocational education subcommittee reported on its meeting about raising Thai students' competitiveness in the PISA assessment, with the agencies concerned invited to explain their projects.
it: The United Kingdom's education system (British Council Thailand)
Proposals on competitiveness (PISA) from the education and vocational education subcommittee

te: Drugs in schools, a seminar on education innovation, and a second weekly meeting
se: The education and vocational education subcommittee reported progress on proposals to prevent and solve drug problems in schools in the upper northeastern provinces, gathering data such as on children who have left school. The committee considered holding an academic seminar, “Education Innovation for the Future”, and agreed to meet twice a week, adding Tuesdays at 14.00 to follow the subcommittees' work.
it: Progress of proposals on preventing drug problems in schools (education and vocational education subcommittee)
Academic seminar “Education Innovation for the Future”
Extra meeting day: Tuesdays at 14.00

te: Preparing a visit to the United Kingdom, and proposals to put research to real use
se: The committee prepared a bilateral meeting and study visit to the United Kingdom on 2–8 March 2026 to learn about managing vocational education, turning research into commercial innovation and using digital technology in classrooms. The higher education subcommittee reported on ways to promote the use of research, and the committee made proposals to the government, such as asking regulators to open testing spaces for new innovations with some rules relaxed.
it: Preparing the bilateral meeting and study visit to the United Kingdom (2–8 March 2026)
Work of the higher education subcommittee: putting research to use
Policy proposals to the government, such as innovation testing spaces

te: Educational opportunities for children in risk areas on the Thai–Cambodian border
se: According to the meeting notice, the agenda was measures to support educational opportunities and care for children and young people in risk areas along the Thai–Cambodian border, including students preparing for university entrance, with the Secretary-General of OBEC and the chair of the Council of University Presidents of Thailand invited, and the work of the subcommittees. The summary will be added after the Senate publishes it.
it: Support for the education and care of children in risk areas on the Thai–Cambodian border and students preparing for university entrance
Work of the subcommittees

te: Putting research to real use, and concern for schools along the border
se: The higher education subcommittee reported on its meeting about promoting the use of medical, health, agricultural and food research for both commercial and public benefit, and about obstacles such as rules and regulations and the incentive system for researchers. The committee expressed concern about the situation in the disputed Thai–Cambodian border area, which forced schools along the border to stop teaching, and agreed to consider a field visit to find ways to help students. It also heard the Office of the Basic Education Commission (OBEC) on its criteria for budget support for school buildings where space is lacking.
it: Promoting the use of research (higher education subcommittee)
Effects on schools along the Thai–Cambodian border
OBEC budget support for school buildings

te: Study topics for fiscal year 2027 and the draft programme for a study visit to Chon Buri
se: The meeting considered 7 topics the subcommittee will study in fiscal year 2027: 1) unequal access to higher education for disadvantaged learners, people with disabilities and those without money, with a proposal for systematic support to local higher education institutions and community colleges; 2) management and good governance in higher education institutions after they became autonomous universities, such as the selection of executives, transparency in the use of budgets and long procedures for academic positions, with proposals to study the effects of the change in status, to review budget allocation so that it reflects need and value, and to encourage discussion in the meeting of university presidents; 3) a lifelong learning system, with higher education institutions as learning centres for all ages (upskill and reskill); 4) building specialist strengths in higher education institutions and reducing overlapping courses through strategic budget allocation; 5) STEM manpower, with incentives starting at secondary level and cooperation with industry; 6) start-up entrepreneurs, with higher education institutions as business incubators and legal mechanisms that make joint ventures with the private sector easier; and 7) the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on higher education. The meeting also considered the draft programme for a study visit and seminar in Chon Buri, including visits to higher education institutions in the area and a seminar to hear the views of government, local bodies and the private sector on the subcommittee's study results.
it: Study topics for fiscal year 2027 (7 topics): access to higher education, good governance in higher education institutions, lifelong learning, specialist strengths, STEM manpower, start-up entrepreneurs and the impact of AI
Draft programme for a study visit and seminar in Chon Buri
